data.text:
🟦 MORNING BRIEFING: While You Slept — March 23, 2026

⭕️ BREAKING —

• President Trump suspends strikes on energy infrastructure in Iran, announces “productive conversations” toward ending hostilities; planned strikes on Iranian power infrastructure paused.

• Iran claims U.S. backed down — Iranian officials say Washington retreated under threat of attacks on regional energy and power grids.

• Conflicting narratives on talks — Tehran denies negotiations with the U.S., framing Trump’s move as retreat.

• Strikes continue across Iran — Explosions reported in Tehran, Yazd, Shiraz, Bushehr, and Ahvaz targeting IRGC and defense-linked sites.

• Hormuz tensions shift — Oman mediates safe passage talks as oil prices drop below $100 following pause in escalation.

• Missile fire persists — Iran continues launches toward Israel; sirens across central and southern regions overnight.

U.S. —

• Global security alert issued — State Department urges Americans worldwide to exercise increased caution amid escalating conflict.

• LaGuardia disaster — Plane collision with fire truck in New York kills at least two and injures dozens.

• Domestic incident in Los Angeles — Multiple people injured in stabbing attack in downtown area.

• Pentagon media ruling — Court forces restoration of press credentials for major outlets.

ISRAEL —

• Missile barrages continue — Multiple Iranian launches trigger alerts across Jerusalem, Ashkelon, and central Israel; most intercepted.

• Civilian debris injuries reported — Falling missile fragments wound at least one in the UAE and cause damage in Israel.

• Gaza operation ongoing — IDF eliminates armed Hamas cell in central Gaza.

• Northern front active — Hezbollah rocket attacks and anti-tank fire continue; IDF expands ground operations and seizes weapons caches.

• Leadership coordination continues — Israeli cabinet prepares for next phase amid U.S. diplomatic push.

IRAN —

• Nuclear site evacuation prep — Russia’s Rosatom plans phased evacuation of Bushehr nuclear plant staff.

• New assassination reported — Senior Iranian official targeted and killed in northern Tehran.

• Energy warfare threats escalate — Iran threatens to strike power grids and infrastructure across the region.

• Military pressure continues — Missile and ammunition depots destroyed along Ahvaz coast; IRGC naval sites hit.

LEBANON —

• Hezbollah claims attacks on Israel — Rocket salvos reported targeting northern positions and IDF units.

• IDF strikes crossings and infrastructure — Continued targeting of Litani River crossings and Hezbollah logistics routes.

• Weapons caches seized — Israeli forces capture anti-tank missiles and equipment in southern Lebanon.

MIDDLE EAST —

• UAE under sustained attack — 7 ballistic missiles and 16 drones intercepted in latest wave; nearly 1,800 drones engaged since war began.

• Bahrain reports major interceptions — 147 missiles and 282 drones destroyed since start of hostilities.

• Qatar LNG strike confirmed — Advanced Iranian missiles successfully hit energy infrastructure, evading defenses.

• Kurdistan targeted — Iran launches missile and drone strikes into northern Iraq.

• Regional alliances shifting — Gulf states reassess security ties with the U.S. amid ongoing attacks.

EUROPE —

• UK increases Jewish community protection — Police boost security following antisemitic arson attack in London.

• Starmer pushes de-escalation — UK signals it will not be drawn into war despite rising tensions.

• Energy crisis deepens — Europe faces declining gas supplies as global disruptions intensify.

GLOBAL —

• Oil market volatility continues — Prices swing sharply amid shifting war dynamics and Hormuz uncertainty.

• Asia faces fuel shortages — Vietnam, Bangladesh, and the Philippines risk running out of oil within weeks.

• China urges restraint — Warns conflict could spiral into uncontrollable regional war.

• Cuba hit by blackouts and fires — Ongoing power instability worsens domestic conditions.

• Aviation and maritime risks rise — Incidents and threats increase across global transport networks.

That's your morning briefing.

Traffic Advisory 📢 
Heads up, Goodyear. Maricopa County will begin pavement rehabilitation work starting Monday, March 23, on portions of Perryville Road, Lower Buckeye Road, Citrus Road and Yuma Road. Work is expected to continue through May, Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with limited weekend work possible. Drivers should plan for lane reductions, flagging operations and extra travel time in the area. Please slow down, follow posted traffic control signs and watch for crews. For questions, contact Maricopa County Department of Transportation at 602-506-3342 or MCDOTprojects@maricopa.gov
